prose.summary: The aluminium window frames meet the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. This results in an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 76101000, Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. This results in an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED. Note that the CEPA rate applies only to Basic Customs Duty; other import charges such as IGST are still payable.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) and at least 45% value addition (VA) on a free-on-board (FOB) basis. The final manufacture check passed, confirming the last step took place in the UAE, and the minimal operations check passed, showing the work went beyond simple operations. The CTSH check passed because all three non-originating inputs are classified outside subheading 761010, and the VA check passed with a build-down of 49.0%, exceeding the 45% threshold. Therefore the product meets the rule of origin.

notes.text: A product that only undergoes the minimal operations listed in Article 3.5.1 (e.g., simple assembly, packaging, labelling) does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.
Electronic certificates from the UAE issuing authority are accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit by the importer or customs broker.

The duty estimate is based on the shipment value given (100,000 AED). India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; no conversion is done.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The '+' in the product-specific rule is interpreted as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
The origin checks (final manufacture and minimal operations) are based on the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' (used in the build-up method) are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not state whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A product that only undergoes the minimal operations listed in Article 3.5.1 (e.g., simple assembly, packaging, labelling) does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating, but the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.

For a retrospectively issued certificate, the agreement says box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5-year requirement governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
Electronic certificates from the UAE issuing authority are accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit by the importer or customs broker.
